claims.quote: one of over 500 known solar systems in the entire Milky Way galaxy
claims.claim: [Our solar system is] one of over 500 known solar systems (planetary systems) in the Milky Way galaxy.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: The NASA Exoplanet Archive already listed 5,438 confirmed exoplanets on 18 May 2023, nine days before this video was published (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/2023news.html), and now lists 6,354 confirmed planets across roughly 4,700 planetary systems (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/counts_detail.html). 'Over 500' is true only as a lower bound and understates the known count by roughly an order of magnitude, which is the kind of understatement that reverses the impression the sentence is built to give.

claims.quote: about 4.5 billion years ago when a cloud of interstellar gas and dust collapsed, resulting in a solar nebula, a swirling disc of material
claims.claim: The solar system formed about 4.5 billion years ago when a cloud of interstellar gas and dust collapsed into a solar nebula, a swirling disc of material.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'Our solar system formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a dense cloud of interstellar gas and dust. The cloud collapsed... When this dust cloud collapsed, it formed a solar nebula, a spinning, swirling disk of material.' https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/solar-system-facts/ The mechanism matches exactly; 4.5 versus NASA's 4.6 is rounding of the same ~4.57 billion year radiometric age, so the figure is right to the precision 'about' claims.

claims.quote: The solar system is located in the Milkyways Orion star cluster.
claims.claim: The solar system is located in the Milky Way's Orion star cluster.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: The location is right and the object class is wrong. NASA: 'Our Sun lies near a small, partial arm called the Orion Arm, or Orion Spur, located between the Sagittarius and Perseus arms.' https://science.nasa.gov/resource/the-milky-way-galaxy/ The Orion Arm is a spiral arm structure, not a star cluster (a gravitationally bound group of stars formed together); NASA's solar system overview likewise places us in 'one of the Milky Way galaxy's spiral arms' (https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/). There is no 'Orion star cluster' the Sun belongs to.

claims.quote: Only 15% of stars in the galaxy host planetary systems
claims.claim: Only 15% of stars in the Milky Way host planetary systems.
claims.label: false
claims.basis: Every published occurrence rate is far higher. Kepler-based forward modelling puts about 72% of FGK stars as hosting at least one planet in the 0.5 to 500 day, 0.5 to 16 Earth-radii range (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1907.07773); a narrower 3 to 300 day, 0.5 to 10 Earth-radii window alone gives 0.441 +/- 0.019 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.02840); NASA states that about half of Sun-like stars could host a rocky habitable-zone planet (https://www.nasa.gov/missions/kepler/about-half-of-sun-like-stars-could-host-rocky-potentially-habitable-planets/) and that Kepler established 'there are more planets than stars in the galaxy'. 15% is below the rate for a single restricted period range, let alone all planets.

claims.quote: and one of those stars is our own sun
claims.claim: Our Sun is one of the galaxy's stars that hosts a planetary system.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Trivially true and stated by NASA in the same breath as the planet count: 'Our solar system has eight planets, and five dwarf planets.' https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/ The Sun hosts a planetary system by definition. Same sentence as S4 and the opposite truth value: the fraction is wrong, the example attached to it is right.

claims.quote: Revolving around the sun are eight planets.
claims.claim: Eight planets orbit the Sun.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'Our solar system has eight planets, and five dwarf planets.' https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/ Eight has been the count under the IAU definition since 2006.

claims.quote: The planets are divided into two categories based on their composition terrestrial and Jovian.
claims.claim: The eight planets are divided into two compositional categories, terrestrial and Jovian.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: The terrestrial/Jovian split is the standard two-way compositional classification, with the Jovian group subdividing into gas giants and ice giants, which is exactly how the video then uses it. NASA's planets overview draws the same line, 'terrestrial planets because they have solid surfaces' against outer planets that 'have swirling gases above a core', and subdivides the outer four: 'Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants. Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.' https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets/ A three-way taxonomy is also common, so this is a defensible simplification rather than an error.

claims.quote: Terrestrial planets, including Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars, are primarily made of rocky material.
claims.claim: The terrestrial planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, and they are primarily made of rocky material.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA groups the same four inner worlds as the rocky planets with solid surfaces, against the outer four which 'don't have hard surfaces'. https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets/

claims.quote: Their surfaces are solid
claims.claim: The terrestrial planets have solid surfaces.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA uses solid surfaces as the defining property of the group: terrestrial planets are 'known as terrestrial planets because they have solid surfaces'. https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets/

claims.quote: they don't have ring systems, they have very few or no moons, and they are relatively small
claims.claim: The terrestrial planets have no ring systems, very few or no moons, and are relatively small.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: All four known planetary ring systems belong to the giant planets; no inner planet has one (https://www.planetary.org/articles/rings-of-the-solar-system). Moons: Mercury 0, Venus 0, Earth 1 ('Earth is the only planet in our solar system with only one moon', https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/), Mars 2, Phobos and Deimos, against 274 confirmed for Saturn alone (https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/moons/facts/). Three moons across four planets is 'very few or no moons' on any reading.

claims.quote: The smallest and closest to the sun is Mercury
claims.claim: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and nearest to the Sun.' https://science.nasa.gov/mercury/facts/

claims.quote: which has the shortest orbit in the solar system at about three earth months
claims.claim: Mercury has the shortest orbit in the solar system, about three Earth months.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: Mercury 'speeds around the Sun every 88 days... faster than any other planet' (https://science.nasa.gov/mercury/facts/). 88 / 30.44 days per average month = 2.89 Earth months, so 'about three earth months' is right. 'In the solar system' also survives the wider reading: the record-holding short-period asteroid 2021 PH27 orbits in 114.6 days and has 'the second smallest semi-major axis of any known object orbiting the sun, behind Mercury' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_PH27), so no known body orbits the Sun faster.

claims.quote: Venus is the hottest planet
claims.claim: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: its thick atmosphere 'traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect, making it the hottest planet in our solar system'. https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/

claims.quote: with temperatures of up to 867 degrees Fahrenheit
claims.claim: Venus reaches surface temperatures of up to 867 degrees Fahrenheit.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: 867 F is 464 C, the long-standing NASA mean surface temperature for Venus; NASA's current Venus page gives 'approximately 872 degrees Fahrenheit (467 Celsius)'. https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/ The two figures differ by 5 F, well inside the stated precision, and 867 is a low-side rather than an inflated number.

claims.quote: due to an atmosphere of carbon dioxide and extensive lava flows
claims.claim: Venus's extreme surface temperature is caused by its carbon dioxide atmosphere and by extensive lava flows.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: Half right, and the wrong half is presented as a co-cause. NASA attributes the heat to one mechanism: 'Its thick atmosphere traps heat in a runaway greenhouse effect', with an atmosphere that 'is mostly carbon dioxide' (https://science.nasa.gov/venus/venus-facts/). Lava flows are not a heat source for the present surface temperature: Venus is uniformly ~464 C day and night, poles included, which is what a greenhouse atmosphere produces and what localised volcanism cannot. Venus does have extensive volcanic plains, so the words are not invented, but naming them as a cause of the temperature is a real error. Same sentence as S14 and the opposite truth value: the number is right, the explanation attached to it is not.

claims.quote: The water systems on this planet helped create the only known environment in the universe capable of sustaining life.
claims.claim: Earth's water systems helped create the only known environment in the universe capable of sustaining life.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA on Earth: 'It's the only place we know of inhabited by living things', and 'Earth is unique in that most of our planet is covered in liquid water, since the temperature allows liquid water to exist for extended periods of time.' https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/ 'Only known' is a claim about the state of knowledge and is correct as of labeling; no life has been confirmed anywhere else.

claims.quote: Mars, might have also supported life about 3.7 billion years ago, when the planet had a watery surface and moist atmosphere
claims.claim: Mars might have supported life about 3.7 billion years ago, when it had a watery surface and a moist atmosphere.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Curiosity found mudstones and wave ripples in Gale crater dated to about 3.7 billion years ago, showing long-lived lakes open to the atmosphere and therefore a dense enough atmosphere for unfrozen surface water: JPL, 'NASA's Curiosity Rover Team Confirms Ancient Lakes on Mars' (https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/nasas-curiosity-rover-team-confirms-ancient-lakes-on-mars/), and the habitable-lake reading at https://astrobiology.nasa.gov/news/ancient-lake-on-mars-was-hospitable-enough-to-support-life/. The date and the water are established; the claim is correctly hedged to 'might have supported life', since habitability, not life, is what the evidence shows.

claims.quote: The Jovian planets include gas giants Jupiter and Saturn, and ice giants Uranus and Neptune.
claims.claim: The Jovian planets are the gas giants Jupiter and Saturn and the ice giants Uranus and Neptune.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants. Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.' https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/planets/

claims.quote: The gas giants are predominantly made of helium and hydrogen
claims.claim: The gas giants Jupiter and Saturn are predominantly made of hydrogen and helium.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA on Jupiter: 'The composition of Jupiter is similar to that of the Sun, mostly hydrogen and helium.' https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/facts/ Saturn is likewise hydrogen and helium dominated.

claims.quote: the ice giants also contain rock, ice, and a liquid mixture of water, methane, and ammonia
claims.claim: The ice giants Uranus and Neptune contain rock, ice, and a liquid mixture of water, methane and ammonia.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA on Uranus: it consists of 'a hot dense fluid of icy materials, water, methane, and ammonia, above a small rocky core', which is '80% or more' of the planet's mass. https://science.nasa.gov/uranus/facts/ Neptune has the same interior structure.

claims.quote: All four Jovian planets have multiple moons.
claims.claim: All four Jovian planets have multiple moons.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Saturn alone has '274 confirmed moons, far more than any other planet', and the solar system has '421 officially recognized moons orbiting planets' (https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/moons/facts/); NASA counts 95 IAU-recognised moons at Jupiter (https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/facts/). Uranus and Neptune both have dozens of known moons. Only three moons in the whole solar system orbit non-Jovian planets, so 'multiple' holds for all four with an enormous margin, and the exact counts moving does not threaten it.

claims.quote: Sport ring systems have no solid surface and are immense.
claims.claim: [All four Jovian planets] have ring systems, have no solid surface, and are immense.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: All four giant planets have ring systems, including Jupiter's, found by Voyager 1 in 1979, and the narrow dark rings of Uranus and Neptune (https://www.planetary.org/articles/rings-of-the-solar-system, https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/facts/). No solid surface: NASA, 'As a gas giant, Jupiter doesn't have a true surface. The planet is mostly swirling gases and liquids.' The transcript garbles a word here ('Sport' for 'sport', i.e. possess), but the three assertions are unambiguous and all hold.

claims.quote: The largest Jovian is also the largest planet in the solar system, Jupiter.
claims.claim: Jupiter is the largest Jovian planet and the largest planet in the solar system.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'It's the largest planet in our solar system, if it were a hollow shell, 1,000 Earths could fit inside.' https://science.nasa.gov/jupiter/facts/

claims.quote: Saturn, the solar system's second largest planet
claims.claim: Saturn is the solar system's second largest planet.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: Saturn is 'the sixth planet from the Sun, and the second-largest planet in our solar system.' https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/

claims.quote: Its signature rings are wide enough to fit between earth and the moon
claims.claim: Saturn's rings are wide enough to fit in the gap between Earth and the Moon.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA gives Saturn's ring system as extending 'up to 175,000 miles (282,000 kilometers) from the planet' (https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/). The mean Earth to Moon distance is about 384,400 km, so 282,000 km fits inside it with about 100,000 km to spare. Note the measurement basis: NASA's figure is the outward extent of the ring system, and comparing it to a centre-to-centre distance is the standard popular framing of this comparison.

claims.quote: but are fairly a kilometer thick
claims.claim: Saturn's rings are barely a kilometre thick.
claims.label: plausible
claims.basis: NASA gives the main rings a 'vertical height... typically about 30 feet (10 meters)' (https://science.nasa.gov/saturn/facts/). Read as an upper bound, 'less than a kilometre thick' is true and is the point being made; read as an estimate, a kilometre overstates the typical thickness by about two orders of magnitude, though vertical structures at some ring edges do reach a few kilometres. The transcript word is garbled ('fairly' where the audio is almost certainly 'barely'), so the honest band spans confirmed to misleading depending on which reading a verifier takes, and the wide tolerance records that rather than hiding it.

claims.quote: The slightly bigger of these ice giants
claims.claim: Uranus is the slightly bigger of the two ice giants.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'Uranus is slightly larger in diameter than its neighbor Neptune, yet smaller in mass', with an equatorial diameter of 51,118 km (https://science.nasa.gov/uranus/facts/) against Neptune's 49,528 km (https://science.nasa.gov/neptune/facts/). A 3.2% difference is 'slightly bigger' by diameter. Measurement basis matters: by mass Neptune is the larger of the two, and the video's word is 'bigger', which reads as size.

claims.quote: is famous for rotating on its side
claims.claim: Uranus is famous for rotating on its side.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: Uranus has an axial tilt of 97.77 degrees. NASA: 'Uranus is the only planet whose equator is nearly at a right angle to its orbit... This unique tilt makes Uranus appear to spin sideways, orbiting the Sun like a rolling ball.' https://science.nasa.gov/uranus/facts/

claims.quote: Neptune, the outermost planet in the solar system
claims.claim: Neptune is the outermost planet in the solar system.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet in our solar system.' https://science.nasa.gov/neptune/facts/ True since Pluto's 2006 reclassification as a dwarf planet.

claims.quote: and also one of the coldest
claims.claim: Neptune is one of the coldest places in the solar system.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: The two ice giants are the coldest planets: NASA records a minimum atmospheric temperature of 49 K (-224.2 C) for Uranus, the coldest measured planetary atmosphere in the solar system (https://science.nasa.gov/uranus/facts/), and describes Neptune as 'Dark, cold, and whipped by supersonic winds' at the greatest distance from the Sun (https://science.nasa.gov/neptune/facts/). The hedged form 'one of the coldest' is what the evidence supports; 'the coldest' would not be, since Uranus records the lower temperature.

claims.quote: Orbiting the terrestrial planets is the asteroid belt
claims.claim: The asteroid belt orbits the terrestrial planets.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: The main belt orbits the Sun, not the terrestrial planets, and it lies outside them rather than around them. NASA: 'Most asteroids can be found orbiting the Sun between Mars and Jupiter within the main asteroid belt.' https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/asteroids/ A listener could take the phrasing as loose shorthand for 'lying beyond the inner planets', which is why this is misleading rather than flatly false, but as stated it asserts the wrong central body.

claims.quote: a flat disc of rocky objects full of remnants from the solar system's formation, from microscopic dust particles to the largest known object, the dwarf planet Ceres
claims.claim: The asteroid belt is a flat disc of rocky objects left over from the solar system's formation, ranging from microscopic dust to its largest object, the dwarf planet Ceres.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'Dwarf planet Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, and it's the only dwarf planet located in the inner solar system' (https://science.nasa.gov/dwarf-planets/ceres/facts/), and asteroids are formation leftovers ranging down to 'bodies that are less than 33 feet (10 meters) across' (https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/asteroids/). Note NASA calls Vesta the largest asteroid, which is consistent: Ceres is the largest object in the belt but is classified as a dwarf planet rather than an asteroid, exactly as the video says. Same sentence as S31 and the opposite truth value: the belt is described correctly right after being placed incorrectly.

claims.quote: Another disc of space debris lies much further out and orbits the Jovian planets the icy Kuiper Belt.
claims.claim: The Kuiper Belt is a disc of space debris much further out that orbits the Jovian planets.
claims.label: misleading
claims.basis: The Kuiper Belt orbits the Sun and lies beyond Neptune's orbit, outside the Jovian planets rather than around them. NASA: it is 'a doughnut-shaped region of icy objects beyond the orbit of Neptune', with some objects 'one billion miles (1.6 billion kilometers) beyond Pluto'. https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/kuiper-belt/ The same wrong central body as S31, repeated one structure out; 'lies much further out' is right.

claims.quote: the Kuiper Belt is also home to dwarf planets such as Pluto
claims.claim: The Kuiper Belt is home to dwarf planets such as Pluto.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'The Kuiper Belt is home to Pluto and Arrokoth', and its residents include 'dwarf planets and some comets'. https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/kuiper-belt/

claims.quote: is the birthplace of many comets
claims.claim: The Kuiper Belt is the birthplace of many comets.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA lists comets among Kuiper Belt residents and describes the region as left over from the solar system's formation (https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/kuiper-belt/); the Kuiper Belt and the scattered disc beyond it are the source region for short-period comets, while long-period comets come from the Oort Cloud, which the video itself goes on to describe. 'Many' rather than 'all' is the accurate quantifier and is what was said.

claims.quote: Beyond the Kuiper Belt is the Oort Cloud, a vast spherical collection of icy debris.
claims.claim: Beyond the Kuiper Belt lies the Oort Cloud, a vast spherical collection of icy debris.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA: 'a vast, extremely distant spherical shell of icy bodies', which 'lies far beyond Pluto and the most distant edges of the Kuiper Belt', described as a 'thick bubble of distant, icy debris'. https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/oort-cloud/facts/ One caveat holds the tolerance open: NASA also calls it 'a theorized group of icy objects', never directly observed, so the description is the accepted model rather than a measured structure.

claims.quote: It is considered the edge of the Solar system since that is where the gravitational and physical influences of the sun end.
claims.claim: The Oort Cloud is considered the edge of the solar system because that is where the Sun's gravitational and physical influence ends.
claims.label: confirmed
claims.basis: NASA's own answer to where the solar system ends gives this as one of three definitions and attaches it to exactly this criterion: 'if you judge by the stopping point of Sun's gravitational influence... the solar system would end at the Oort Cloud'. https://science.nasa.gov/resource/where-is-the-edge-of-the-solar-system/ The other two boundaries NASA offers, the outermost planet and the heliopause where the solar wind stops, are much closer in, so 'considered the edge' is one accepted convention rather than the only one, which is why the band stays open to plausible.

claims.quote: make it a special place to call home
claims.claim: The solar system's particular configuration of planets and other objects makes it a special place to call home.
claims.basis: A value judgement about the solar system, not a factual assertion with a truth value to check.
